title: arXiv Trending Physics — Daily (2026-10-23 batch)
global_caveat: This is an inferred notable-paper ordering, not an official arXiv trending chart. Citation evidence for papers this recent is limited; usable Semantic Scholar citation metadata was not available at the snapshot, so no citation totals or momentum claims are used.

sections.title: Experimental evidence of forward energy transfer induced by core-edge coupling in multiscale tokamak turbulence
sections.authors: F. Chen, Z. M. Shen, N. Sun, P. Li, Z. Y. Qiu et al.
sections.abstract: The authors combine collective Thomson scattering and Doppler backscattering measurements to report forward transfer of turbulent energy from ion to electron scales associated with an edge-originating quasi-coherent mode in a tokamak core.
sections.claimed_result: The authors interpret measured cross-scale correlations as forward energy transfer driven by coupling between an edge quasi-coherent mode and broadband core turbulence; the full paper reports signatures across EAST campaigns.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; multichannel collective Thomson scattering and radially localized Doppler backscattering on EAST, with nonlinear simulations for interpretation.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say simulations do not reproduce all observed spectral detail; missing impurity-density and temperature profiles limit quantitative comparison. They also report that the improved-confinement regime requires careful density and impurity control.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete experimental result pairs two complementary diagnostics; the full paper reports recurrence of the signatures in more than 1,000 EAST discharges across 2021–2026.

sections.title: Measurements of the branching fractions of Λc⁺→ΛK⁺π⁰ and Λc⁺→ΛK⁺η decays at Belle and Belle II
sections.authors: Belle and Belle II Collaborations; M. Abumusabh, I. Adachi, A. Aggarwal, Y. Ahn, H. Aihara et al.
sections.abstract: Using 1.55 ab⁻¹ of Belle and Belle II data, the collaborations improve the relative branching-fraction measurement for Λc⁺→ΛK⁺π⁰ and report the first observation of Λc⁺→ΛK⁺η.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a Λc⁺→ΛK⁺η branching fraction of (6.20 ± 0.25 ± 0.31 ± 0.30)×10⁻⁴ and find it larger than current SU(3)-flavor-symmetry predictions; the third uncertainty comes from the reference branching fraction.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; Belle and Belle II e⁺e⁻ collision samples at KEKB and SuperKEKB, totaling 1.55 ab⁻¹.
sections.unique_caveat: Absolute branching fractions inherit uncertainty from the world-average reference mode; the authors also note sub-combination mass-spectrum differences from phase-space simulation that may reflect unresolved intermediate resonances.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The combined collider dataset yields a first observation above 10σ and a more precise measurement of a related decay; both are specific, checkable experimental milestones.

sections.title: Detection of Solar-like Oscillations and Granulation at Infrared Wavelengths using JWST
sections.authors: Angharad Weeks, Daniel Huber, Timothy R. Bedding, Jared Splinter, Hans Kjeldsen et al.
sections.abstract: JWST/NIRISS time-series observations of the exoplanet host WASP-121 reveal solar-like oscillations and granulation in infrared light, with amplitudes that decrease with wavelength but depart from simple blackbody scaling.
sections.claimed_result: The authors use JWST observations of the F6V star WASP-121 to detect infrared oscillations and granulation and report wavelength-dependent amplitudes inconsistent with a simple blackbody scaling.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; JWST/NIRISS SOSS time-series photometry of WASP-121, analysed with a Gaussian-process framework.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is based on one star; the paper says the time series is too short to robustly measure the lower-frequency supergranulation component.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A first infrared detection of two stellar-variability signals bridges stellar convection and exoplanet time-series analysis; the arXiv abstract page notes resubmission to ApJ Letters following a favourable referee report.
sections.comment: Recently resubmitted to ApJ Letters following favourable referee report.

sections.title: A cosmic filament catalog for COSMOS-Web Data Release 1 across 0.5 < z < 3.5
sections.authors: Qiaoyang Hao, Tao Wang, Weishan Zhu, Hong Guo, Peng Wang et al.
sections.abstract: The authors combine COSMOS-Web Data Release 1 photometric-redshift probability distributions with a DisPerSE-based workflow to release a catalog of 12,523 cosmic filaments and 136,210 segments over 0.5 < z < 3.5.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report extracting 12,523 filaments from COSMOS-Web DR1, with parameters tuned against TNG-based mock catalogs to reduce discrepancies between projected and 3D structures.
sections.evidence_type: Observational and computational; COSMOS-Web DR1 photometric-redshift PDFs, DisPerSE extraction, and TNG simulation mock catalogs.
sections.unique_caveat: Filament identification relies on photometric-redshift probability modeling and calibrated projection from 3D mock structures; the extracted catalog is not a direct spectroscopic 3D map.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A substantial catalog, segment catalog, and probability maps are released; the work is cross-listed across cosmology, galaxy astrophysics, and instrumentation/methods and has a journal DOI.

sections.title: Odd radio circle J1555+2726: Observational evidence for shock re-acceleration of fossil plasma
sections.authors: L. Bruno, B. Koribalski, R. P. Norris, A. Ivleva, T. Venturi et al.
sections.abstract: Multi-frequency LOFAR, uGMRT, and MeerKAT maps of the odd radio circle J1555+2726 show spectral curvature and radial flattening that the authors interpret as likely shock re-acceleration of pre-existing relativistic plasma.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find a convex spectral curvature and flattening toward the ring, and argue that a mixture of electron populations with different spectra is consistent with re-acceleration of fossil plasma.
sections.evidence_type: Observational; LOFAR, upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope, and MeerKAT radio imaging and spectral-index maps.
sections.unique_caveat: The re-acceleration scenario is an interpretation of the spectral morphology; standard shock acceleration of thermal particles plus ordinary spectral ageing does not explain the observed shape.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The analysis combines three radio facilities over 50–1284 MHz and reports resolved spectral properties; the result is cross-listed in galaxy and cosmology astrophysics.

sections.title: From phase analysis to phase tracking: a robust approach to atomic-scale strain mapping
sections.abstract: Geometric phase tracking analysis follows displaced Bragg reflections pixel by pixel and, on 13,795 simulated and experimental atomic-resolution images, lowers the reported failure rate relative to conventional geometric phase analysis.
sections.claimed_result: The authors propose GPTA, which tracks local reciprocal-space peaks and report improved strain/dislocation maps under large strain, rotation, and dynamical-scattering extinction.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; algorithm benchmarked on simulated and experimental atomic-resolution microscopy images.
sections.unique_caveat: The numerical advantage is reported for the tested image set and imaging conditions; broader performance across microscopy instruments and acquisition regimes remains to be established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper benchmarks 13,795 images and reports failure-rate reduction from 27% to 11.5% and up to 335-fold better accuracy in tested cases.

sections.title: Photometric classification and out-of-taxonomy detection of ZTF transients with FLARE
sections.authors: Argyro Sasli, Felipe Fontinele Nunes, Xuanrui Zhang, Dimitrios Kourtesis, Saina Nikmehr et al.
sections.abstract: FLARE classifies ZTF transients and flags events outside known classes; a simulated review loop recovers 83% of held-out out-of-taxonomy examples after inspecting 15% of the alert stream.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that blind anomaly detection recovers few out-of-taxonomy events at a 1% false-alarm rate, while a simulated iterative review process improves recovery and benefits from confirmed examples being added as a new class.
sections.evidence_type: Computational; machine-learning classification and anomaly detection evaluated on ZTF light curves and a simulated review loop.
sections.unique_caveat: The out-of-taxonomy evaluation set contains 53 objects, and the 83% recovery figure comes from a simulated review process rather than a prospective controlled deployment trial.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Evaluated on 10,497 spectroscopically confirmed ZTF transients plus 53 outside-taxonomy objects, with explicit false-alarm/recovery metrics; the abstract says the module runs in production on ZTF's Fritz/SkyPortal system.

sections.title: A 13 Year Black Hole Microlensing Survey in Omega Centauri
sections.authors: Zack Freeman, Maximilian Häberle, Anil Seth, John Zaris, Matthew Whitaker et al.
sections.abstract: A search of nearly 200 Hubble single-band images spanning 13 years finds no convincing stellar-mass black-hole microlensing candidates in Omega Centauri, and releases the photometric dataset.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report no convincing candidates and, using their simulated-event completeness, find that zero events were expected in this dataset, contrary to earlier expectations.
sections.evidence_type: Observational and computational; Hubble Space Telescope images, synthetic microlensing events based on Omega Centauri Monte Carlo simulations, and a neural-network selection stage.
sections.unique_caveat: The null result depends on the assumed simulation-based event population and the survey's single-band sensitivity/completeness; it does not establish that the cluster contains no stellar-mass black holes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The 13-year HST baseline, explicit synthetic-event completeness analysis, and released photometric dataset make this a testable null search.

sections.title: Metasurface engineering of transient photothermal responses for vibrational imaging at living interfaces
sections.authors: Zhibin Hu, Tianrun Zhang, Jiayu Ding, Pengcheng Fu, Ziyang Huang et al.
sections.abstract: The authors use resonantly engineered metasurfaces for mid-infrared photothermal imaging and report submicrometre chemical maps of nanoparticles and living cells, including lipid conversion across a cell membrane.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that metasurface-enhanced transient heating with visible-light readout resolves spatially distinct enzymatic lipid-conversion signals in living cells.
sections.evidence_type: Experimental; metasurface-driven mid-infrared photothermal imaging with visible-light detection on nanoparticles and biological cells.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract establishes a proof-of-concept demonstration but does not quantify detection limits or validation across cell types; those are needed to assess generality.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete optical-instrument method is demonstrated on living-cell chemical change, with a stated submicrometre mapping capability linking photonics and biological measurement.
